title: Lockstep pin never touches the production terminal_statuses const — the claimed guard layer cannot bite on const drift
evidence:
// server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam:1061-1063
/// package (AR-RC13 guard, #607 item 5) — this is the same decision, encoded
/// for DB-string rows; the lockstep unit test pins the two together.
const terminal_statuses: List(String) = [
  "form_completed",
  "manual_recorded",
  "unreachable",
  "refused",
  "objected",
  "partial",
  "failed",
  // v2-reserved voice terminal — harmless to include.
// server/test/application/application_detail_handler_test.gleam:593-601
pub fn terminal_statuses_lockstep_with_shared_truth_test() {
  let terminal = [
    "form_completed",
    "manual_recorded",
    "unreachable",
    "refused",
    "objected",
    "partial",
    "failed",
    "completed",
  ]
detail: The test iterates a hand-written duplicate list; the private const is unreachable from the test module (imports are only application_detail_handler/application/sql). Removing "partial" from the const or adding a new terminal string passes every test while the timeline silently diverges — the exact drift class this guard targets.
recommended_fix: Expose the const (pub) or add `pub fn is_terminal_status_string(String) -> Bool` wrapping const + status_from_string + shared fn, consumed by build_lifecycle_entries, and have the lockstep test iterate the real list.

title: outcome_from_string is orphaned in production and now duplicates the optional mapping's 15 arms
detail: Repo-wide grep shows zero non-test callers after the encoder switched to outcome_from_string_optional (only shared tests still call it). Its doc claims "non-wire callers" that do not exist, and its 15 arms now duplicate the new function's — every future outcome addition must update both.
recommended_fix: Implement outcome_from_string as `case outcome_from_string_optional(v) { Some(o) -> o; None -> OutcomeUnreachable }` so one mapping exists, and correct the doc comment to drop the false non-wire-callers claim.

title: Amendment register claims §8.2 was amended in place with the unknown-outcome rule, but §8.2 contains no such content
evidence:
**Amended in place:** AD-11 (Prevents + hook semantics — see below), §8.2 (hooks contract
doc: unknown-outcome rule, #607 item 2).
// §8.2 as it actually reads (lines 1043-1047):
### 8.2 State rules the API computes (so screens don't)

`can_record_manual`: any non-terminal status. `can_substitute_referee`: terminal `objected` /
`unreachable`. `can_retry`: `failed`. Per-reference display copy ("awaiting referee", "declined
contact", "unreachable after 3 attempts — try calling them yourself") derives from
detail: The register lists §8.2 as amended with the unknown-outcome rule, but the section only describes the three hook booleans. The named rule exists solely in the shared module doc; the canon's claimed in-place amendment was never written.
recommended_fix: Add the unknown-outcome rule to §8.2: hooks derive from status only; an unrecognised outcome encodes absent (null), never the OutcomeUnreachable fallback.
